subjects.note: run_subjects.py (owner, 2026-11-07): non-math subjects on the subscription, one system prompt per subject and mode (prompts/subject/solve.md or aids.md, filled from prompts/subject/profiles/<slug>.md). solve: questions whose own solution is missing or a Gemini one get a full solution, answer key, hint and takeaways; the old solution is never sent. aids: questions with the book's own solution get an answer key, hint and takeaways built on it; the book's solution stays. The answer key (pipeline/answer_key_spec.md) goes to questions.answer_key and, for aids, the takeaways to questions.takeaways (app migration 008). Only subjects listed in profiles are in scope.
subjects.tiebreak_note: Owner 2026-11-07: when two solves disagree with the stored answer, a third solve at tiebreak_effort (stored answer never sent) decides. Agreeing with the stored answer, it is accepted as usual; agreeing with an earlier solve, it is accepted and its answer replaces the stored one (old value kept in pipeline.db provenance as answer_before_replace); agreeing with neither, human review.
subjects.review_model_note: Owner 2026-11-10: the book flags of the image run (217) and later review questions go to Claude Fable 5.2 at medium effort; earlier review solves were Fable 5.1 and keep that attribution.
subjects.review_effort_note: Owner 2026-11-08 15:31: 'Continue with fable medium instead' after the high-effort review solves used up several accounts' session limits; replies already received keep their high-effort attribution.
subjects.review_note: Owner 2026-11-08 ('Do the human review parts with fable on high'): a question in human review gets a full, blind solve (solve mode, the subject's prompt; neither the book's solution nor the stored answer is sent) by review_model at review_effort, and that solve is final. Agreeing with the stored answer, it is accepted as usual; disagreeing, it is accepted and its answer replaces the stored one (old value kept in pipeline.db provenance as answer_before_replace). A reply that fails the checks is retried with the checks' feedback, up to review_max_attempts review solves; after that a person decides. Questions still waiting for their tie-break are left until the tie-break is judged. run_subjects.py adjudicate sends them.
subjects.figure_ok_ids_note: Owner 2026-11-10: the questions the figure rule skipped although they carry no figure and need none (they ask for a sketch, or 'given below' points at a table that is present). Each was read; they are sent like any other question. The 7 that do point at a missing figure were deleted from the app.

submissions_closed_note: Owner decision 2026-10-21: no more API submissions; the 585 retries and 514 unsolved questions stay as they are. run.py submit/loop refuse to send while this is true (dry runs still work).

subscription.note: run_sub.py: the same solver (prompts, model, effort, max_tokens, checks) on the Claude subscription through Claude Code in print mode, one fresh process per question. Scope: the math sources below, in priority order (retries first), for every question whose own solution is missing or a Gemini one and that has no generated solution yet. submissions_closed does not apply: it is the API lock.
subscription.hard_note: Owner decision 2026-11-04 (after the trip-up research): the 'hard' sources (olympiad/research, undergraduate competitions, famous-but-tricky puzzles) run at high effort with a 128k output cap, and every question in them is redone, including the ones the API solved at medium. Proof-heavy graduate/exam sources (Kaczor & Nowak, Berkeley, Cambridge Tripos, Stirzaker & Grimmett, Mladenovic, Oksendal) were considered and left at medium.

subscription.redo_ids_note: Owner decision 2026-11-04: questions the API solved (at medium) before the missing-reference rewrite made their text self-contained (Burton 38, Kaczor & Nowak 30; 35 others whose only change was an encoding repair are left alone). Each is redone once at its source's effort; a question counts as done once a subscription reply exists for it.
subscription.api_leftover_ids_note: Owner decision 2026-11-06: the API run's unfinished questions (status retry or pending with an API batch id; the API is not used any more) go through the subscription, whatever their source or solution kind: 219 rejected once (they continue at attempt 2 with the API's feedback) and 160 canceled or never sent. Left out: 1308 and 13587, which already have a generated solution (Fable 5.1 max; Opus medium, passed). 10 more were deleted from the app (12094, 12758, 12900, 13828, 16258, 16260, 16364, 16663, 17803, 17811).
subscription.figure_ok_ids_note: Owner 2026-11-10: math questions the figure rule skipped although they carry no figure and need none (they ask for a sketch, 'figure' means a shape or 'figure out', or 'given below' points at a table that is present). Each was read; they are sent whatever their source or solution kind, as the API run would have, after everything else. The 7 that do point at a missing figure were deleted from the app.
subscription.image_ids_note: Owner 2026-11-10: 'send the 51'. The book-solved image questions of sources outside this scope (Erikson 23, Creative Puzzles 16, Stirzaker 4, Yaglom 4, Mosteller 3, Schwarz 1), which the API run skipped for their images. Sent with their images, whatever their source or solution kind, after everything else; the book solution stays and the reply fills the generated solution. 14258 already has a generated solution (max effort), so 50 go out.
subscription.effort_by_id_note: Owner 2026-11-11: 'Yes, try it at high'. A question named here is solved at this effort whatever its source gets; a lower-effort earlier attempt is redone from attempt 1, as for effort_by_source. 14306 (Erikson) was cut at the output cap twice at medium.

prices_note: USD per million tokens, standard tier, from the Claude API reference cached 2026-10-06; verify against the pricing page. Batch requests are billed at batch_discount times these. cache_write is the 1-hour TTL rate (2x input).
judge_here_note: Owner 2026-11-07: a small judge round (at most judge_here_max replies waiting) runs here with run.py judge, which backs up the app DB first; bigger rounds go to the other machine through remote_judge.py.
attach_images_note: Owner 2026-11-10: solve the questions with images. run_sub.py and run_subjects.py send a question that names images with \includegraphics together with them (in aids mode the book solution's too): the same text, then each image after a line naming its command, as one stream-json message. The system prompts are unchanged (format rule 11 already asks for a figure to be described in words), and Claude Code's wrapping is the accepted one. Questions skipped for an image before this go again; one whose image file is missing, or whose text points at a figure it does not carry, is still skipped. False restores the old rule.
